title: Graph extension computes etale compact support on sheaves
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $u:U\to X$ a separated quasi-compact etale morphism of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], and $u=pj$ a compactification with $j:U\to Z$ open and $p:Z\to X$ proper. The canonical graph-extension natural transformation $a_c:u_{\Sigma!}\to p_*j_!$ of [def-f7-etale-compactification-graph-map] is an isomorphism on constant-$A$ module sheaves. No Noetherian or global compactness condition is imposed on $U,X$. The scheme, morphism, and functor notions used here are those of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension].

source.place: Tag 0F4Y (lemma-separated-etale-shriek) and Tag 0F52 (lemma-compactify-f-shriek-separated); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F4L supplies graph extension. The proof below gives the geometric-fibre verification of the explicit map.

proof.text: Construct the graph map as in [def-f7-etale-compactification-graph-map]. The graph is clopen: it is open inside the base change of j because it is an etale diagonal, and is closed as a section of the proper map q. The projection is identity on this component and zero on its complement.

Base change pulls this decomposition back to the corresponding graph and complement. The projection therefore commutes with base change, component by component. Etale sum exchange is the adjunction-preserving comparison of restriction functors. Mate pasting and transposition under the proper inverse-image/direct-image adjunction identify the base change of a_c with the graph map on the base-changed compactification. The equality is checked on the two sheaf components before passing to any derived category. For the open-extension component, the source API openImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeMap supplies compatibility with ordinary exchange, and unit_map_openImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeMap_app supplies its adjunction normalization.

At a geometric point apply proper base change in degree zero to the previous square. The etale geometric fibre is a finite disjoint union of points, and every section on it has proper support. It is clopen in the proper fibre, since its finitely many rational points are closed. Restriction identifies the two sides with the finite sum and finite product of the stalks. Equivalently, Mathlib IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite gives finiteness of the fibre map directly; the finite-etale sum/direct-image comparison and the clopen comparison compute these same sections.

The graph projection sends a sheet germ to itself on its component and to zero on every other component. Thus the stalk map is the canonical finite sum-to-product map, which is invertible also for an empty index set. The sum-stalk formula fixes this identification on every summand. Conservative geometric stalks detect isomorphisms; naturality of the constructed graph map gives the claimed functor isomorphism. The clopen-product calculation may first be made after forgetting the module structure; all component maps are linear, and the module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms.
